_comment: This file is the canonical, version-controlled record of the branch-protection
rule applied to the 'main' branch of github.com/GanTechProject/VinayakFortune.
Re-applying: gh api -X PUT repos/GanTechProject/VinayakFortune/branches/main/protection --input branch_protection.json
Reading:    gh api repos/GanTechProject/VinayakFortune/branches/main/protection
If the fields below change, update both this file and the rule on GitHub.
POLICY: required_approving_review_count is 0. The 'require PR' gate stays on
(no direct pushes); the 'CI status checks' gate stays on (post-unblock); only
the unsatisfiable 1-approval human-review gate is dropped. Rationale: on a
single-human repo, GitHub's review model hard-blocks the PR author from
approving their own PR, so required_approving_review_count: 1 is structurally
unsatisfiable (the only writer is the only candidate reviewer, and they are
always the PR author). With 0 approvals, the author can merge their own PR
through the GitHub UI/API, and the post-unblock CI workflows become the
actual review-quality gate (ci-hello-world + docs-lint contexts).
When a second human joins with write access, raise the count to 1 to restore
the human-review gate. This is a one-line edit to required_approving_review_count
(0 -> 1) followed by a PUT of this file to the live API.
POLICY: require_code_owner_reviews is true. The 'CODEOWNERS' file (installed
by PR #55, 2026-07-28, at 442bbea) declares @GanTechProject as the owner for
default + /docs/ + /services/auth-svc/ + /services/hello-world/ +
/.github/workflows/. With this flag on, any PR that touches a CODEOWNERS-
covered path triggers a code-owner review request from the CODEOWNERS bot.
On a single-human repo where all CODEOWNERS rows point to the same human
who is also the PR author, the rule is trivially 'satisfied' (the only
owner is the only author), and the human merges via the GitHub web UI
bypass button as repo admin. The flag is therefore an audit-trail /
documentation signal, not a hard block on solo-repo PRs.
When a second human joins, the flag becomes a real gate: code-owner reviews
from the human NOT named as author are required to merge. The PATH-1
sequence (PR #42, 2026-07-27) flipped required_approving_review_count: 1 -> 0
because the 1-approval human-review gate was the FIRST unsatisfiable rule
on a solo repo. This require_code_owner_reviews flag is the SECOND
unsatisfiable rule (it was satisfiable from the moment CODEOWNERS landed
in PR #55, so the live API was flipped on 2026-07-28 in a follow-up PUT
after PR #55 merged). The canonical reflects this live state from this PR.
If a third human joins and the team wants to enforce BOTH review gates,
the live API would need: required_approving_review_count: 1 +
require_code_owner_reviews: true + at least two human CODEOWNERS rows that
are NOT the PR author. Until then, the flags are independently toggleable
but only the 0-approval + code-owner-true pair is currently satisfiable.
LEGACY: the Option 3 cycle (DELETE reviews rule, merge, PUT back) was the
pre-Path-1 merge dance that worked around the unsatisfiable 1-approval rule.
scripts/merge_pr{18,23,...,41}_cycle.sh are HISTORICAL AUDIT RECORDS of cycles
that ran under the old policy and are NOT updated by Path 1. Going forward,
the conductor merges via the GitHub UI/API directly (with 0 approvals trivially
satisfied) or via scripts/merge_prN_cycle.sh if they prefer the scripted form
(the script's drift check is updated per-PR to expect the new count).
STATUS-CHECKS SEQUENCING: the required_status_checks.contexts list MUST
reference workflow names that already exist in .github/workflows/ on the
branch. The classic branch-protection API does not let you DELETE just the
status-checks rule (no sub-endpoint exists for it, unlike the reviews rule).
So the safe sequence is: (1) the conductor pastes the workflow files directly
into `main` via the GitHub web UI (per PHASE_C_POST_UNBLOCK_ROADMAP.md §2 and
RUNBOOK_after_paste.md step 4; the OAuth `workflow` scope blocks the bot from
pushing the branch), (2) the conductor pushes a third (no-op) commit to
trigger an actual workflow run (GitHub Actions does not run on the commit
that adds the workflow file itself), (3) the orchestrator runs
`bash scripts/post_paste_cycle.sh` to PUT the contexts list. Putting the
contexts in this file BEFORE the workflows have run will not block pushes,
but the PUT will silently keep `contexts: []` because the live API will not
register the names until at least one workflow run completes. As of v1.2 the
two workflows (ci-hello-world, docs-lint) are pending human-attested addition
via the GitHub web UI (OAuth workflow-scope blocks the CLI), so this file
lists contexts: [] until they land and the post-paste cycle runs.
If migration to GitHub Repository Rulesets is desired (a separate API
that decouples 'PR required' from 'PR review required'), the ruleset endpoint
supports the finer-grained control.
API gotcha: setting required_pull_request_reviews to null on this endpoint
disables BOTH the 'require PR' and 'require review' rules; they are not
independently toggleable on the classic branch-protection API. Do not null
this field unless you intend to remove the PR requirement entirely.
